flaw: A closure repair could be presented as evidence that hierarchy works.
cause: The factorial question and the hierarchy comparison test different mechanisms.
repair: Freeze separate closure/substep contrasts and the corrected-hierarchy comparison with distinct decision rules; a success in one does not decide the other.
required_evidence: Prospective protocol naming each contrast, endpoint, practical threshold, comparison family, and terminal decision before outcomes are inspected.

flaw: Known external forces and a matching integrator do not establish algorithmic novelty.
cause: The proposed successor diagnoses a model contract using established numerical and physical ingredients.
repair: Describe a bounded diagnostic contribution; compare closest prior mechanisms in the literature ledger and make no architecture novelty or state-of-the-art claim.
required_evidence: Dated primary-source comparison and claim wording limited to what the retained diagnostic and learned comparisons actually establish.

flaw: The transition can remain misspecified even after an external-force term is added.
cause: Wall forces are piecewise functions of position and velocity, drag depends on velocity, and supplied actions alone are not the full external impulse.
repair: Specify wall, drag, action, masks, units, and evaluation state exactly; recompute the declared closure on the current predicted state during integration.
required_evidence: Force-free, drag-only, wall-contact, and applied-force sanity cases; single-object parity where no learned internal force exists; retained boundary cases.

flaw: Substepping can multiply an impulse incorrectly or evaluate forces at the wrong state.
cause: A force and an observation-step impulse have different units; one and four semi-implicit steps have different position updates.
repair: Freeze whether the learned output is force and when it is recomputed; multiply force by the actual substep duration and advance the predicted state consistently; keep observation dt fixed at 0.05.
required_evidence: Hand-computable constant-force cases for the declared substep settings, multistep state checks, and agreement of serialized configuration with executed integration.

flaw: The closure or substep contrast could include unrecorded architecture or training changes.
cause: Changing closure, integration, width, initialization, objective, data, and stopping together prevents attribution.
repair: Use the same local central-force family in the closure-off/on by one/four-substep factorial; freeze all other differences and retain paired initial states and randomness where meaningful.
required_evidence: Complete planned factorial, explicit parameter/configuration differences, shared dataset identities, and separately reported main contrasts and interaction.

flaw: The candidate could win because it receives more physical information.
cause: Known wall/drag coefficients or geometry, and generator constants shared by wall and contact laws, can reveal useful information unavailable to a control.
repair: Declare every known and learned coefficient; supply the same environment information to all competitive learners and identify any different functional prior; intentional closure-off cells remain explicit ablations.
required_evidence: Input/parameter information table, implementation inspection, and equally informed learned-control configurations.

flaw: Simulator replay could be counted as learned-model success or as a fair trained baseline.
cause: The full known-law simulator has access to the exact generating dynamics and needs no statistical learning.
repair: Keep the simulator as a labeled parity/reference oracle outside learned-model superiority decisions; distinguish an unfitted prior-only control from each fitted learned control.
required_evidence: Separate oracle/prior/learned report rows, disclosure of known coefficients and fitting procedure, and decision code that uses only the declared competitive controls.

flaw: A hierarchy may only approximate a force that a simple mean-based model expresses exactly.
cause: The generator's harmonic all-pairs term equals -kappa * (x_i - mean(x)) using the ordinary masked mean position; mass-weighted pooling is a different statistic.
repair: Include the predeclared learned analytic-mean/simple parametric control; fit its unknown quantities on training/development data only and give it the shared external closure and integrator.
required_evidence: Algebra/reference check of the mean identity, fitted-parameter provenance, retained control predictions, and the corrected hierarchy's paired comparison against this control.

flaw: Beating a radius-limited local model would not isolate hierarchy-specific value.
cause: All-pair interactions or direct global context may remove the same information restriction with simpler computation.
repair: Compare the corrected hierarchy with the equally informed full-pair/global control and simple parametric control; keep the hierarchy always on and add no routing mechanism.
required_evidence: Matched-interface control results and a predeclared hierarchy decision that cannot pass solely by beating the local factorial reference.

flaw: A direct position bypass could explain a comparison attributed to hierarchy or closure.
cause: Historical models predict different objects, including bounded state corrections and direct position residuals.
repair: Specify one chronological force/state/integrator interface for the successor comparisons; enumerate any intentionally different control parameterization; keep historical namespaces separate.
required_evidence: Dimensions, equations, initialization, losses, forward/training/inference order, and source-level correspondence for every included model.

flaw: Low trajectory error would not identify a unique physical law or prove broad causal understanding.
cause: A known noiseless generator and fixed environment permit shortcut or nonunique fitted explanations over limited trajectories.
repair: Limit conclusions to predictive and algorithm-intervention effects in the declared generator; disclose which laws are supplied and which quantities are learned.
required_evidence: Fitted parameters and predictions with uncertainty where applicable; explicit statement that general law identification is not tested.

flaw: A boundary-aware transition cannot claim unrestricted translation equivariance with a fixed arena.
cause: Translating particles without translating walls changes their wall forces.
repair: Restrict symmetry claims to internal central forces and transformations valid for the declared fixed arena; use no arbitrary geometry or dt shifts in this study.
required_evidence: Property checks under stated masks and transformations, with wall geometry included in any transformation that purports to transform the whole physical problem.

flaw: Zero action does not imply conserved total momentum or energy.
cause: Walls and drag remain external/dissipative effects, and the prediction's external forces depend on its own evolving state.
repair: Check internal pair momentum/torque separately from total externally forced evolution; report physical residuals against the correct declared balance and do not reuse the predecessor's action-only bound for the corrected model.
required_evidence: Internal-force sum checks, external-balance diagnostics, and metric definitions that distinguish action-free, externally force-free, and dissipative scenes.

flaw: Padding or out-of-scope properties could change aggregation or dynamics.
cause: Variable object counts affect means and denominators; the historical simulator and MR paths use different mass floors.
repair: Keep N at most eight and live masses at least 0.7; require positive radii, Boolean masks, zero padding, and identical live-object semantics across models; reject inputs outside the frozen contract.
required_evidence: Dataset validation, padding-invariance and variable-count cases, extrema in retained dataset metadata, and identical per-scene masks across controls.

flaw: Generic-scene conservation or symmetry tests do not establish universal guarantees.
cause: Tied anchors, empty groups, small restriction weights, inertia floors, and discrete neighborhood changes can alter the asserted algebra.
repair: State the exact tie/empty-group/floor behavior and the scope of each theorem; retain targeted degenerate cases without silently changing predecessor semantics.
required_evidence: Finite outputs/gradients where defined, mass-accounting and force/torque residual checks, and explicit exceptions or failed cases for unsupported guarantees.

flaw: An executable model may fail to train or optimize the stated objective.
cause: Masking, discrete neighborhoods, clamp boundaries, force scaling, or serialization may disconnect or alter useful gradients.
repair: Check meaningful state/action/parameter gradient paths and exact reload behavior; use numerical checks away from declared nondifferentiable boundaries and retain those boundaries as limitations.
required_evidence: Finite nonzero gradients for reachable trainable components, small hand-verifiable cases, reload/resume agreement, and a bounded end-to-end training dry run.

flaw: Teacher-forced or one-step gains may not survive autoregressive evaluation.
cause: Loss horizon, noise, checkpoint selection, and rollout exposure can favor models differently.
repair: Freeze the same applicable data exposure, loss weights, curriculum, noise policy, validation criterion, and free-rollout evaluation; record any model-specific fitting procedure explicitly.
required_evidence: Training/validation traces, selected checkpoint identities, and per-horizon free-rollout predictions on declared development and protected splits.

flaw: Extra parameters or extra tuning could explain an observed advantage.
cause: Neural widths and simple parametric models differ in capacity and optimization needs.
repair: Record actual trainable counts and tuning trials; use the protocol's meaningful capacity controls without inactive padding; do not handicap the simple model to force nominal parameter equality.
required_evidence: Per-model parameter counts, actual mismatch, fitting/tuning ledger, and interpretation separating mechanism from remaining capacity differences.

flaw: Four substeps can improve error by doing more work.
cause: The factorial deliberately changes integration work and may also multiply neural evaluations; equal updates are not equal compute.
repair: Report the numerical intervention as including its computational cost; freeze resource ceilings and do not turn equal-update accuracy into an efficiency claim.
required_evidence: Per-cell executed updates, substep/model-call counts, measured training/inference cost, and explicitly bounded accuracy/cost interpretation.

flaw: A short-budget result cannot rank asymptotic model quality.
cause: Optimization speed, sensitivity, and simple-control fitting can differ materially within the fixed budget.
repair: Use one bounded development budget with disclosed calibration choices; retain learning curves and report fixed-budget results without asserting convergence or universal ordering.
required_evidence: Budget and trial ledger, achieved updates, learning curves, fitting diagnostics for simple controls, and an explicit remaining convergence limitation.

flaw: Repeated redesign until a positive score would invalidate the intended research pipeline.
cause: Outcome-driven changes can consume unbounded compute and select favorable hypotheses or seeds.
repair: Freeze finite model/trial/update/wall-time budgets and stopping rules; preserve every attempt; a material post-result change receives a new successor version.
required_evidence: Prospective budget, complete attempts/deviations ledger, stopping reason, and no undisclosed architecture or seed replacement.

flaw: Run configuration may not describe the data actually used.
cause: Default Experiment construction exposes only part of Physics, while prepared datasets can carry separately specified generation choices.
repair: Bind complete Physics, generator source, object/property/action policies, dtype, shapes, units, split domains, and tensor-content hashes; verify prepared data agree with the protocol.
required_evidence: Retained DatasetSpec/records and actual tensor hashes, checked contract extrema, unique trajectory identities, and source snapshot of generation.

flaw: Protected outcomes could become another development set.
cause: Predecessor outcomes are already observed, and repeated evaluation or selection among protected seeds would leak information.
repair: Use separately identified fresh protected seeds, freeze model/configuration/selection/analysis before their outcomes are inspected, and record the first reveal; no protected result may guide redesign within v1.
required_evidence: Split and seed registry, disjointness checks, freeze identity and reveal log, and separation of development versus protected reports.

flaw: Many timesteps or model seeds could create artificial statistical precision.
cause: Timesteps share a trajectory, model seeds share a generated dataset, and intentionally paired interventions may reuse initial scenes.
repair: Define the experimental unit and preserve pairing; summarize within trajectory/data-seed clusters before treating clusters as independent; identify deliberate sharing across factorial cells.
required_evidence: Per-trajectory metrics with data/model/scene IDs and documented aggregation that does not count timesteps or nested model seeds as independent datasets.

flaw: A reported improvement could result from an aggregation or denominator choice.
cause: Pooled RMSE, mean scene RMSE, object-weighted errors, and equal-weighted OOD splits are different estimands.
repair: Predefine coordinate/horizon/object/scene/split aggregation, practical effect and near-zero denominators; use the same mask and metric implementation for every model.
required_evidence: Independent metric sanity cases and analysis regenerated from retained per-trajectory predictions using the frozen estimator.

flaw: The best split, control, seed, or interaction could be promoted after inspection.
cause: The factorial, hierarchy controls, physical diagnostics, and horizons create multiple opportunities for a favorable result.
repair: Freeze primary contrasts and the comparison family; apply the declared multiplicity rule or keep secondary results descriptive; do not replace the primary endpoint with a favorable stratum.
required_evidence: Complete comparison table, all declared splits/seeds, explicit secondary/exploratory labels, and unaltered decision code.

flaw: A small protected sample may not resolve a practically meaningful effect.
cause: Few independent data seeds limit inferential resolution even when there are many trajectories or model seeds.
repair: Use the frozen unit-aware uncertainty procedure and disclose its limitations; allow MIXED or INCONCLUSIVE outcomes and do not claim powered external confirmation.
required_evidence: Intervals or clearly labeled descriptive summaries, actual independent-unit count, and comparison with the predeclared practical threshold.

flaw: Dropping unstable, timed-out, or missing cells could improve a reported score.
cause: Successful cells alone are not the intended experimental matrix.
repair: Freeze treatment of nonfinite predictions, exceptions, exhausted budgets, and missing outputs; retain partial evidence and distinguish a valid poor model from a genuinely invalid experiment.
required_evidence: Complete planned-versus-observed grid, failure/status logs, failed predictions where representable, and the protocol's conservative terminal decision.

flaw: Apparent efficiency may reflect measurement scope or host conditions.
cause: Warmup, validation, graph construction, threading, memory allocators, and concurrent load can change measured cost.
repair: Freeze hardware/thread/precision/warmup and measurement scope; record training and inference separately and state exactly what the memory measurement includes.
required_evidence: Measured wall time and memory with method/environment records, repetitions where budget permits, and no hardware-general efficiency claim.

flaw: A small sparse-looking model may still perform quadratic work.
cause: Dense distance construction and coarse topology work can dominate despite sparse retained edges; N at most eight cannot establish asymptotic scaling.
repair: Report the actual implemented operations and restrict this study to small N; make no large-N or subquadratic-efficiency claim.
required_evidence: Source-level complexity description and bounded measured costs; larger-scale evidence remains explicitly outside v1.

flaw: Summary-only artifacts may prevent later error localization or reanalysis.
cause: Aggregate metrics lose trajectories, pairing, failures, selected checkpoints, and hidden preprocessing details.
repair: Retain predictions/targets or faithfully regenerable inputs with identities, per-scene metrics, trained parameters/checkpoints, configs, logs, environment, and all failures within the declared storage budget.
required_evidence: Complete manifest and an artifact map covering every cell and every numerical claim; documented handling of partial runs.

flaw: A checksum-valid package can still omit planned experiments or contain an inconsistent summary.
cause: Hash verification alone does not validate the protocol grid, run status, or analysis arithmetic.
repair: Use a new-study verifier that checks required paths, complete planned cells, dataset/source identities, terminal statuses, finite metrics, and recomputed summaries; label integrity-only checks accurately.
required_evidence: Tamper/missing-cell/schema checks where meaningful and regeneration of the study summary from retained raw metrics; explicit distinction from scientific replay.

flaw: Recorded HEAD could identify different code from the code that produced the result.
cause: Uncommitted edits, reused checkpoints, changing dependencies, or concurrent development can break source/result binding.
repair: Snapshot/hash the actual executed model, generator, trainer, analysis, and protocol; record commit plus dirty state and environment; isolate run outputs from subsequent edits.
required_evidence: Exact source snapshots/digests and run metadata sufficient to reconstruct execution without treating a base commit as the executed working tree.

flaw: A manually edited table or plot could drift from the retained measurements.
cause: Formatting and selective exports can change numerical values, ordering, uncertainty, or omitted failures.
repair: Generate all numerical tables and scientific figures from the frozen analysis outputs; maintain claim to experiment to raw artifact to analysis to figure/table links.
required_evidence: Regeneration commands, generated tables/figures, numerical cross-checks, and no unexplained difference from the retained source metrics.

flaw: An author-run test suite or integrity check is not independent reproduction.
cause: The same implementation, environment, and analyst can share unnoticed errors.
repair: Request a separate adversarial review and clean-environment replay where practical; record exactly what was independently checked and leave unreplayed scientific claims qualified.
required_evidence: Independent review receipt and reproducible comparison of regenerated analysis or bounded runs; no blanket independence claim without that evidence.

flaw: Internal controls do not establish superiority over official learned-physics methods or external tasks.
cause: Official GNS/EGNN/SEGNN and multiscale sources are pinned but unintegrated; public external datasets do not share the current small-object interface.
repair: Use the internal controls for this diagnostic and retain official-baseline/external-dataset integration as unresolved; do not call the internal graph an official reproduction.
required_evidence: Clear model provenance and scope labels; faithful official baseline and task-valid external results would require a separately frozen future study.

flaw: Small noiseless synthetic success would not establish broad physical generalization.
cause: The study fixes the arena, observation dt, known environment, dimensionality, state observations, and N at most eight; missing/noisy observations and unseen simulator families are not covered.
repair: Limit OOD claims to the exact prespecified synthetic shifts and protected seeds; add no arbitrary geometry/dt shift, perception, router, large-N, or general law-identification claim.
required_evidence: Complete declared-shift results and an explicit untested-regime list; any broader claim needs a new version and evidence boundary.

flaw: A successor cannot quantify how much of the historical MR loss came from the diagnosed obstruction.
cause: The original 75-run MR report, summary, manifest, trajectories, checkpoints, and exact source/result archive were not recovered in the bounded checkout/archive search.
repair: Preserve predecessor no-advance and source-reported counts without reconstructing results from prose; treat new diagnoses and comparisons as independently versioned evidence.
required_evidence: Original archive would be required for aggregate retrospective attribution; the new study must instead retain its own complete source/result binding.

flaw: A complete diagnostic is not automatically a submission-ready research release.
cause: Repository ownership/license/authorship metadata and any future external-source redistribution terms remain separate unresolved requirements.
repair: Record these as release limitations without blocking authorized local diagnostic work; publish no unsupported license, authorship, venue-readiness, or external-data claim.
required_evidence: Owner-provided release metadata and verified applicable terms before the corresponding release claim; v1 otherwise remains an experimental diagnostic.

flaw: A favorable successor cell could erase negative history or be portrayed as a perfect model.
cause: The user goal includes improvement, but the pipeline requires valid terminal conclusions and preservation of failed hypotheses.
repair: Classify each predeclared question on its own evidence; preserve negative, mixed, inconclusive, invalid, and failed outcomes; qualify supported findings to this scope and version any material new hypothesis.
required_evidence: Final claim-evidence ledger, unchanged predecessor artifacts/decisions, full deviations and failures, and a defensible terminal disposition without an indefinite positivity search.
